# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The incumbent is timing-feasible at WNS 0.445 ns and WHS 0.208 ns, using 16 LUTs and 34 FFs on the xc7a35tcpg236-1 at a 10 ns period. The editable top is only a wrapper around a frozen CRC core, so changing the top requires replacing that instance with equivalent logic; once timing is feasible, promotion requires strictly fewer LUTs than the incumbent.

## Hypothesis

Replacing the core’s eight-step CRC recurrence with a factored, parallel GF(2) XOR transform may reduce LUT use while preserving the one-cycle registered output and one-byte-per-cycle throughput.

## Instruction for generator

Replace the `crc16_stream_core` instance with top-level state and slot logic, and implement the byte update as a factored parallel XOR network for the CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE polynomial rather than eight serial shift-and-conditional-XOR rounds. Preserve the exact `in_ready` equation, accepted-byte behavior, synchronous active-high reset priority, frame restart on `in_last`, registered output hold during stalls, and minimum accepted-transfer age of one cycle; retain `// @latency 1`. The experiment succeeds only if the unchanged verification gates pass and routed LUT use is strictly below 16, with setup WNS and hold WHS both nonnegative.
